findings.evidence: The declarations at lines 187, 192, and 197 all begin `(e : V ≃L[𝕜] W) (π : ContRepresentation …)`, while the only grep hits at OrthogonalDecomposition.lean:259–261 invoke them with fully qualified names rather than `π.congrEquiv e`.
findings.fix: Put `π` before `e` in all three declarations and update their uses, so the advertised `ContRepresentation` dot notation elaborates; alternatively place an `e`-first API in the continuous-linear-equivalence namespace.
findings.issue: `congrEquiv`, `congrEquiv_toContinuousLinearEquiv` (line 192), and `congrEquiv_apply` (line 197) are in namespace `ContRepresentation` while their first explicit argument is `e : V ≃L[𝕜] W`; thus `π.congrEquiv e` does not match their argument order. This violates the namespace/dot-notation rule for the first explicit argument.

summary: The new transport API is filed for ContRepresentation dot notation, but its argument order makes the continuous linear equivalence the dot receiver.
